cards.explanation: The answer is to stand firm in their freedom. Paul, the apostle writing this letter, says, “It is for freedom that Christ has set us free. Stand firm, then…” (Galatians 5:1). The freedom is already handed over, so the job now is to hold your ground. I dig in on my gold base when somebody tries to shove me around, and that's the picture.

The answer is True. Paul says not to be “…encumbered once more by a yoke of slavery.” (Galatians 5:1). A yoke is the frame that hitches animals to a load, and slavery is the one he doesn't want them back under. Notice the words “once more.” He's warning about something that's out there waiting for them.

The answer is no value at all. Paul says if they let themselves be circumcised, “…Christ will be of no value to you at all.” (Galatians 5:2). There's no half credit and no discount there, friends. He means every word, and he put his own name on it.

The answer is False. Paul says, “Again I testify to every man who gets himself circumcised that he is obligated to obey the whole law.” (Galatians 5:3). One command is not the deal, the whole law is. Paul testifies to this, and I'd listen.

The answer is that they have been severed from Christ. Paul says, “You who are trying to be justified by the law have been severed from Christ…” (Galatians 5:4). Severed means cut off, and Paul chose that word on purpose. He says it plain, and it's a heavy line.

The answer is faith. “But by faith we eagerly await through the Spirit the hope of righteousness.” (Galatians 5:5). Faith is how they wait, and the Spirit is who they wait through. Paul puts both in one short line.

The answer is faith expressing itself through love. “What matters is faith expressing itself through love.” (Galatians 5:6). Faith isn't just something you hold in your head. It shows up in how you love people. Paul says it right after saying neither circumcision nor uncircumcision has any value.

The answer is False. Paul says, “Such persuasion does not come from the One who calls you.” (Galatians 5:8). He asks who obstructed them, but he doesn't hand over a name. He just rules out one source. The One who called them isn't the One tugging them off course.

The answer is the whole batch. Paul says, “A little leaven works through the whole batch of dough.” (Galatians 5:9). Little goes in, and it reaches all of it. I've stamped plenty of dough, and a little bit never stays in its own corner of the bowl.

The answer is that he will bear the judgment. Paul says, “The one who is troubling you will bear the judgment, whoever he may be.” (Galatians 5:10). Whoever he may be, so Paul doesn't name him. That's a serious line, so I'll just let it stand.

The answer is False. Paul asks, “…if I am still preaching circumcision, why am I still being persecuted?” (Galatians 5:11). His question points the other way. He isn't preaching it, and he adds that otherwise “…the offense of the cross has been abolished.”

The answer is True. Paul says, “For you, brothers, were called to freedom; but do not use your freedom as an opportunity for the flesh.” (Galatians 5:13). He puts the warning right alongside the call to freedom. I think he wants them to use that freedom well. Right after, he says, “Rather, serve one another in love.”

The answer is “Love your neighbor as yourself.” Paul says, “The entire law is fulfilled in a single decree…” and then names it (Galatians 5:14). One decree holds the whole thing. That's a lot packed into a short line, friends.

The answer is consumed. Paul says, “But if you keep on biting and devouring one another, watch out, or you will be consumed by one another.” (Galatians 5:15). Notice the if: Paul is talking about what could happen if they keep on biting and devouring one another. That's why he says to watch out.
